hypothesis: Double the task-agnostic uniform corpus reservoir used for prior pretraining from 250000 to 500000 eligible unlabeled SMILES, so each otherwise identical five-epoch artifact learns from broader molecular and token support and is less vulnerable to a weak preparation-seed subsample.
method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb autoregressive SMILES policy optimization
method_thesis: Pretrain an autoregressive SMILES language model on the allowed unlabeled corpus and freeze a copy as the molecular prior. During each objective session, sample complete molecules de novo token by token from a trainable agent, rank the accepted molecules by their observed oracle rewards, and update the agent only on the highest-reward fraction using the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: the squared gap between agent log-likelihood and a target formed from prior log-likelihood plus scaled reward. Excluding low-reward samples from policy updates prevents them from repeatedly pulling the agent back toward the prior, while prior likelihood still regularizes the elite updates; this concentrates the scarce feedback on sequences associated with improvement of final Top-1 without screening a finite molecular pool.

method_tags.learning_mechanism: top-fraction Augmented Hill-Climb updates against a frozen prior policy
method_tags.proposal_mechanism: ancestral token sampling from an online reward-conditioned molecular policy

Then, for each assigned artifact seed, aggregate every unchanged ahc_ancestral_sampling record across its five objective sessions and divide the sum of unique_valid_sequence_count by the sum of completed_sequence_count. Report the three per-seed complete-conditioned yields, their minimum, their arithmetic mean, and their range. applicability_conditions: The unlabeled corpus must contain at least 500000 examples that survive the Parent's unchanged connectivity, character-length, and token-length eligibility rules, and the supplied preparation profile must accommodate the doubled example tensor and training work.

The mechanism is most applicable when a 250000-example uniform reservoir can omit rare but learnable SMILES syntax or chemistry that contributes to valid online ancestral support; a highly redundant corpus supplies little additional information when the reservoir is enlarged.

Improved artifact-seed support requires corpus-sampling variance to be a material part of the Parent's observed variation. If model initialization, minibatch order, or online Search-Seed stochasticity dominates, doubling reservoir coverage may leave the weakest-seed yield unchanged.

Higher complete-conditioned novel-valid yield is an intermediate support result, not proof that the added support contains high-reward chemistry. Node n-b992903add3b increased pooled preparation unique-valid support by 4/768 while reducing three-seed macro score, so final objective utility still requires the registered score comparison.

This intervention does not revisit the refuted input-corruption mechanism in n-2661e5071749: all teacher-forcing inputs and targets remain clean, and the only changed training quantity is the number of uniformly retained unlabeled corpus examples.

Preparation remains strictly label-free and task agnostic, and the existing state-dictionary plus schema-versioned configuration, vocabulary and special-token semantics, model architecture, five-epoch schedule, and all downstream Layers remain unchanged.
research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism did not happen if any preparation with at least 500000 eligible corpus rows trains on a count other than 500000, or if corpus eligibility, uniform reservoir replacement, tokenization, architecture, optimizer, schedule, artifact interface, or run-mode behavior differs from the Parent. With that receipt intact, the support claim is falsified if the minimum three-seed online complete-conditioned novel-valid yield does not exceed the Parent's 0.7832720190434971 minimum. A support increase without the required macro-score increase means the mechanism activated without useful objective transfer.
research_intent.implementation_change: Change only TRAINING_EXAMPLES from 250000 to 500000 in the Parent. Keep the preparation-seed-dependent uniform reservoir algorithm, corpus eligibility windows, tokenizer and vocabulary construction, model dimensions, recurrent dropout, optimizer, learning rate, batch size and ordering rule, five training epochs, prior sampling check, support gate, artifact filenames and schema, and every run-mode Layer byte-for-byte equivalent. The existing preparation start and epoch diagnostics and training_examples configuration field will record the enlarged reservoir; the existing online ancestral-sampling diagnostics supply the registered support measurement.
research_intent.mechanism: Double the task-agnostic uniform corpus reservoir used for prior pretraining from 250000 to 500000 eligible unlabeled SMILES, so each otherwise identical five-epoch artifact learns from broader molecular and token support and is less vulnerable to a weak preparation-seed subsample.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: Parent n-6174d6127af5 trains each prior on only a preparation-seed-dependent 250000-example reservoir, and its three artifacts retain different vocabulary sizes of 74, 76, and 78, prior-check unique-valid rates from 0.8125 to 0.85546875, and online complete-conditioned novel-valid yields from 0.7832720190434971 to 0.8541171385346877. The weakest artifact therefore loses about 7.1 percentage points of online support relative to the strongest, while seed macro scores range from 0.498752613558053 to 0.544472616912355. The checkpoint-selection Child n-b992903add3b improved pooled prior-check support by only 4/768 and reduced macro score by 0.008551034406275007, while the clean-target UNK-corruption Child n-2661e5071749 reduced pooled prior-check support from 0.83984375 to 0.7799479166666666 and macro score by 0.02299792456061167. Those results leave limited seed-dependent corpus coverage, rather than checkpoint publication or noisy-prefix training, as the distinct active-layer behavior addressed here.

applicability_conditions: Confirmed activation applies to the supplied unlabeled corpus under the inherited no-disconnected-SMILES, maximum-140-character, and 3-to-100-token eligibility rules. Each of the three preparations actually retained and encoded 500000 examples, establishing that this corpus has sufficient eligible rows and that the allocated CUDA preparation profile accommodated the doubled tensor and training work.

The supported robustness claim is specifically that, across preparation/search seeds 0 through 2, the weakest complete-conditioned online novel-valid yield rises above the Parent's weak-seed threshold and the three-seed spread narrows. It does not establish a positive paired change on every seed, because seed 0 decreases slightly.

The online result covers the frozen Hard-Five task set, 300 calls per task, batch size 10, 29 adaptive rounds per session, five sessions per seed, and the inherited Augmented Hill-Climb updates. All observed batches filled from one 64-sequence sampling group, but transfer to another objective suite, budget, update schedule, or proposal profile is untested.

Preparation remains label-free and task agnostic in the observed implementation: reservoir selection depends only on the corpus and preparation seed, and the published configurations contain preparation metadata but no task identity, initial oracle observation, or score.

Interface compatibility is supported for schema version 1 with smiles_prior.pt plus smiles_policy.json, unchanged BOS/EOS/PAD/UNK semantics, maximum_tokens=100, model dimensions, and five-epoch schedule. All fifteen downstream sessions loaded their seed-specific artifact and completed normally.

The evidence supports broader and more seed-robust complete-conditioned novel-valid online support, not useful objective transfer. The materially lower three-seed macro mean limits this result to an activation finding unless another setting demonstrates that the added support overlaps high-reward chemistry.

observable_measurements.value: The enlarged-reservoir receipt is complete for all three artifact seeds. The seed-0 smoke preparation reused by the formal seed-0 replica and the direct seed-1 and seed-2 preparation logs each report examples=500000 at training start and in every one of five epoch records. Their published schema-v1 smiles_policy.json files independently record training_examples=500000, training_epochs=5, and training_seed 0, 1, and 2, respectively; their vocabulary sizes are 86, 87, and 83. Each artifact seed then contributed 145 unchanged ahc_ancestral_sampling records, comprising 29 rounds in each of five objective sessions. Seed 0 produced 7,751 unique-valid sequences from 9,268 completed sequences (9,280 sampled), for complete-conditioned yield 0.8363185153215364. Seed 1 produced 7,770/9,236 (9,280 sampled), for 0.8412732784755306. Seed 2 produced 8,036/9,276 (9,280 sampled), for 0.8663216903837861. The three Candidate yields therefore have minimum 0.8363185153215364, arithmetic mean 0.8479711613936177, and range 0.0300031750622497. The registered minimum rises by 0.05304649627803937 over the Parent minimum of 0.7832720190434971, and the arithmetic mean rises from 0.8256655118076925 to 0.8479711613936177 while the range contracts from 0.07084511949119066 to 0.0300031750622497. Paired seed directions are mixed but consistent with the registered weakest-seed claim: seed 0 decreases by 0.0032888625233562507, seed 1 increases by 0.05800125943203349, and seed 2 increases by 0.01220455184909841. Because the enlarged reservoir is verified and the Candidate minimum exceeds the fixed Parent minimum, the pre-registered support increase occurred.

possible_failure_causes: The online-support benefit is not uniform per seed. Candidate seed 0 falls from the paired Parent's 0.8396073778448927 to 0.8363185153215364, while the registered minimum improves because the large gain on seed 1 removes the Parent's weak-artifact tail. Three preparation/search seeds establish the stated minimum comparison but do not show that every enlarged reservoir improves support.

With epochs and batch size fixed, doubling retained examples also approximately doubles the number of pretraining minibatches and total optimization work. The intervention intentionally includes that extra work, but these replicas do not separate benefit from broader corpus coverage versus benefit from additional gradient updates.

The preparation-time 256-draw prior checks also move heterogeneously: Candidate rates are 0.83203125, 0.8359375, and 0.90234375, whereas the Parent rates are 0.8515625, 0.8125, and 0.85546875. The registered online aggregate succeeds, but seed 0's lower static check and online yield show that more retained examples do not guarantee better support for every fitted artifact.

The registered online measurement is taken after reward-conditioned policy updates across five objectives, so it measures how each enlarged prior supports the complete downstream search loop rather than isolating the frozen prior before adaptation. Different objectives, update horizons, or Search Seeds could interact differently with the same prepared artifact.

Improved broad novel-valid support did not transfer to the registered score objective. Candidate replica val_scores are 0.503531196657103, 0.49300753989193, and 0.472389779458323, for arithmetic mean 0.4896428386691187, versus Parent mean 0.5142733351593963; the paired mean change is -0.024630496490277654 rather than the required increase. The mechanism therefore activated, but the added valid support was not shown to contain more high-reward chemistry.

The larger reservoirs produced larger but still preparation-dependent vocabularies of 86, 87, and 83 tokens. This is consistent with broader observed syntax, but the artifacts do not identify which newly retained molecules or tokens caused the weakest-seed support improvement, and a more redundant eligible corpus may provide less benefit.

Three preparation/search seeds establish the stated minimum comparison but do not show that every enlarged reservoir improves support.

With epochs and batch size fixed, doubling retained examples also approximately doubles the number of pretraining minibatches and total optimization work. The intervention intentionally includes that extra work, but these replicas do not separate benefit from broader corpus coverage versus benefit from additional gradient updates.

The preparation-time 256-draw prior checks also move heterogeneously: Candidate rates are 0.83203125, 0.8359375, and 0.90234375, whereas the Parent rates are 0.8515625, 0.8125, and 0.85546875. The registered online measurement is taken after reward-conditioned policy updates across five objectives, so it measures how each enlarged prior supports the complete downstream search loop rather than isolating the frozen prior before adaptation. Different objectives, update horizons, or Search Seeds could interact differently with the same prepared artifact.

Improved broad novel-valid support did not transfer to the registered score objective. applicability_conditions: The unlabeled corpus must contain at least 500000 examples that survive the Parent's unchanged connectivity, character-length, and token-length eligibility rules, and the supplied preparation profile must accommodate the doubled example tensor and training work.

The mechanism is most applicable when a 250000-example uniform reservoir can omit rare but learnable SMILES syntax or chemistry that contributes to valid online ancestral support; a highly redundant corpus supplies little additional information when the reservoir is enlarged.

Improved artifact-seed support requires corpus-sampling variance to be a material part of the Parent's observed variation. If model initialization, minibatch order, or online Search-Seed stochasticity dominates, doubling reservoir coverage may leave the weakest-seed yield unchanged.

Higher complete-conditioned novel-valid yield is an intermediate support result, not proof that the added support contains high-reward chemistry.
